note: Which real robots each driver in drivers/models.json commands, what kind of interface it speaks, and what its strongest counterpart has NOT shown. docs/robot-support.md is generated from this file and models.json (node tools/robot-support.mjs), and tools/robot-support.mjs --check holds it in CI. A robot is named here only if the driver was built for it or run against it; a family the vendor sells that the driver has not met is written as such and not as a supported model. Interface: joint-level (the OS commands joints and the Safety Kernel can clamp them), command-level (the vendor's controller owns the servo loop and the OS sends named motions, so Guest is the ceiling, §59.2), or hosted (another framework's plugin runs inside the driver).

unmeasured: Booster's own simulator and controller: they sit behind a login this repository has no account for, so the DDS service the driver speaks has only ever been Booster's SDK talking to itself
the joints' response, because the counterpart integrates a first-order model: gains, falls and CUSTOM-mode transitions are unseen
timing at rate, and the robot's own safety layers

robots: FAIRINO FR3 (the FR series share the vendor's SDK; only an FR3 was built for)
unmeasured: FAIR INNOVATION's own controller software: their SimMachine is a Windows virtual machine behind a registration wall and has not been run; the vendor's FRRobot client is a second opinion on the wire, not on the controller
servo timing, and how the controller reacts to a collision or a protective stop

robots: Deep Robotics Jueying Lite3 (the X20 is refused by name)
unmeasured: any Lite3 controller: Deep Robotics' own MuJoCo simulator speaks a private UDP layout, not MotionSDK's, so the motion host on the other end was written here
four command codes were read out of the vendor's compiled library and have not been confirmed by the vendor
physics, gains, and the vendor's motion-host modes
the real motor drivers: Unitree's simulator applies the impedance law in physics but does not check the CRC or the motor mode
timing at 500 Hz, the robots' own protection layers, and how a real robot recovers from a fall
roles are left to an operator, so the body binds no cross-robot policy until a person asserts them
the real robot's actuator timing, and the drift a latched hold prevents (AgiBot's simulation was not rebuilt after that fix)

for each body whose stage is alpha, everything the vendor's plugin does: those run against ros2_control's mock components with the vendor's description, or (the ABB IRB 1200) against a controller written here
for every body: timing at rate (the bridge hosts a ResourceManager in-process and the counterparts keep simulated time), and the controller's own safety reactions

bodies.ur5e: Universal Robots UR5e, through UR's own ur_robot_driver
bodies.aubo_i5: AUBO i5, through AUBO's own plugin
bodies.kuka_kr6r900: KUKA KR 6 R900 sixx, over RSI

robots: SO-100 and SO-101 (Feetech), Koch v1.0 and v1.1 and OpenMANIPULATOR-X (Dynamixel) — each class run under the bridge — and the other robots LeRobot's Robot class supports
unmeasured: a servo: LeRobot's own SO-101, Koch and OpenMANIPULATOR-X classes and the makers' SDKs have been run under this bridge (44 checks on Feetech, 68 on Dynamixel), against buses of servos emulated here from LeRobot's control tables. That is a counterpart written in this repository, not the makers' firmware
any LeRobot robot but those three: LeKiwi, HopeJR and Reachy 2 have role tables and have not been run, and OpenArm and reBot have no table

what a servo's error bits mean: the bridge asks each servo's error register and torque every 100 ms and a bit is a fault (F232), but only what the emulators can raise has been injected (an overload on a Dynamixel, any bit on a Feetech), and the makers' lists of what each bit is are not in this tree, so `drivers/fault-vocabulary.json` does not bind them

robots: Pudu service robots, through the vendor's cloud OpenAPI (delivery, cruise, call)
unmeasured: Pudu's real cloud: it needs a developer account, and the account is an owner action
there is no cancel for a delivery in the API, so a stop cannot recall a task in flight (documented in the driver)

robots: any CiA 402 servo drive on CAN that exposes the objects the driver reads (encoder resolution, gear ratio, limits, speed)
unmeasured: any vendor's drive: Lely's CiA 402 slave is a protocol counterpart with mock motion
drive quirks, bus load and timing, homing methods, brake control

robots: the same CiA 402 drives, from the Rust port
unmeasured: any vendor's drive, as for the Python driver
the kernel-bus half needs vcan; a machine without the module reports it not run
every slave either master has met was written here; SOEM, an independent master, was run against those slaves and not against this master
distributed clocks, jitter, and a real network interface

robots: the same drives, from the Rust port
unmeasured: as for the Python driver: no slave or master this repository did not write
Fourier's simulators drive the model directly and expose no RoCS endpoint, so the server is written here (Fourier's own client drives it)
roles are left to an operator, and the real robot's response is unseen

robots: Franka Robotics arms over the FCI (server version 10)
unmeasured: a real Control box: franka-sim is a third party's implementation of the FCI server with physics
1 kHz timing: a Python-paced stream crosses the FCI's discontinuity limits on timing alone (F124), which is why the Rust port is the Host-tier one

robots: Franka Robotics arms over the FCI, from the Rust port
unmeasured: a real Control box, and 1 kHz timing against one: franka-sim keeps simulated time

robots: Boston Dynamics Spot (the quadruped; its arm is not driven)
unmeasured: no Spot simulator exists: the services are written here and driven by Boston Dynamics' own client
lease, power and e-stop behaviour on a real robot, and its fault vocabulary
servo timing: URSim's clock is the host's (F171 found a stall at one jitter period)
protective stops, the safety system, payload and TCP configuration, CB3 arms, and any URCap the site installs

robots: the same UR arms, from the Rust port
unmeasured: as for the Python driver: servo timing, protective stops and the safety system

robots: UFACTORY xArm 7 (each row against UFACTORY's firmware started as that arm)
unmeasured: motors: the firmware runs with none, so no dynamics, brakes or thermal state
the firmware's joint ranges are wider than the vendor's own table on four of the five models, so travel is the narrower of the two: a real controller's ranges have not been read
velocity and torque are not offered, and the controller's collision detection is neither configured nor relied on

robots: ArduPilot multirotors, fixed wings, ground rovers, surface boats and submarines or ROVs (ArduSub), and PX4 multirotors, fixed wings and ground rovers (the driver reads the autopilot and the airframe from the heartbeat)
unmeasured: a real flight controller: SITL is the firmware on a simulated board, with no sensor noise or failure, no motors and no radio link

a real ROV: its thrusters, tether, depth sensor and DVL. The simulated submarine's depth is not a measurement (its pressure sensor reads negative absolute pressure and its depth swings by metres in seconds with nothing commanded), so the vertical axis is held only to what the firmware reads off each stick, which is ArduSub's own RC channels in ArduSub's documented directions, and never to where the vehicle goes

what a stop means under water: `stop_mode` is the operator's and has no default, the driver was measured to enter the named mode and send neutral sticks at once, and nothing was measured of what a vehicle then does in a current, on a tether or under ice
a PX4 boat, submarine or VTOL (refused by name: nothing here has driven one)
a boat's stop: HOLD stops the thrust and not the hull, which has no brake, so the SITL boat's time to rest is a simulated drag and not a vessel's
the vehicle's failsafes in the field, the EKF on real sensors, and everything about a real battery

robots: TurtleBot3 Burger, in ROBOTIS's own Gazebo simulation, and iRobot Create 3, in iRobot's own (neither robot was run); and any ROS 2 mobile base that takes a geometry_msgs Twist or TwistStamped and publishes nav_msgs Odometry: Clearpath Husky and Jackal, TurtleBot 4, AgileX bases, Hello Robot Stretch's base, PAL's TIAGo base, anything on ros2_control's diff_drive_controller or mecanum_drive_controller. Claimed from each maker's documentation: only the two simulations and ros2_control's own controller were run
unmeasured: any named base but the TurtleBot3 Burger and the Create 3, and those only as their makers' simulations: each publishes its odometry with its own QoS, covariance and frames, and some take commands on another topic or through a multiplexer; the driver reads QoS compatibly and refuses to open when either topic is missing or unconnected, which is the right failure and not a measurement of that robot

a base on a floor: mock_components/GenericSystem is never late, never stalled and has no inertia, and Gazebo's differential-drive plugin has an acceleration limit and no slip, a battery or a bumper, so layers 7, 9 and 10 are not reached and 6 only as far as a simulator's physics goes, and a base's bumpers, cliff sensors, e-stop chain and hardware command timeout are the base's
navigation: there is no goto, because odometry drifts and a goal-seeking loop on dead reckoning would be a motion nobody asked for; Nav2 would be another driver

robots: any robot arm whose controller runs a ROS-Industrial simple_message server: Yaskawa Motoman (MotoROS), ABB (abb_driver's RAPID server), FANUC (fanuc_driver), Staubli and others, up to ten joints. Claimed from ROS-Industrial's and each maker's documentation: no controller was run, only a server built from ROS-Industrial's own library
unmeasured: any named robot: which controllers have a server, which ports it listens on, whether it answers a ping, what it does when a second client connects, what it does with a point it cannot reach and with a stop trajectory (the maker's header says a server 'should' stop) are each vendor's, and the driver has no model table because the protocol has no model
a robot's own faults: RobotStatus.error_code is each vendor's number and simple_message defines none, so the fault word carries it verbatim and drivers/fault-vocabulary.json has nothing to cover

an arm on a floor: layers 6, 7, 9 and 10 are not reached; the arm behind the maker's sockets is a straight-line interpolator written here, and a controller's own planner, acceleration limits and safety circuit are the controller's
the controller's e-stop input: the driver's stop is a stop trajectory over TCP, a software stop, and safety.estop.independent is a bench test
